data.reply: Done (v53). Spectators now have arms and idle their own way: some cheer, some wave, some shuffle. When a car is heading at one and under about 0.8 s away, they dive clear, land flat, get up and walk back. It works on every stage.

data.reply: Done (v53). The see-through window now also opens whenever the ground between the camera and your car rises above the car, such as this hillside in the Low camera. The hill opens up around your car and closes again once you're past. It never triggers in the default camera, and in Low it opens about 7-10% of a lap on the hilly stages.

data.reply: Done (v53). I measured it: every vehicle needed 38-40 m/s at the kicker and the pack arrives at 39-44, so there was almost no margin. The gap is now 24 m instead of 30, which clears from about 30 m/s, so a slightly slow or off-line run still makes it. It's still a proper leap.

data.reply: Done (v53). Cliff faces now have crisp rock bands and streaks drawn on steep faces, the ground at the foot of a rise is darker, and the top edge catches the light. The terrain also casts shadows now, so cliffs throw shade on the ground below. This applies on every stage with cliffs and banks; shadows are off on Graphics: Low.

data.reply: Done (v53). The wash used to run alongside the main road 8-12 m below it, so the ground between them hung over it like a bridge. It now climbs up to the main road's level before the two run side by side, with a low bank between them, and meets the junction level.

data.reply: Fixed (v58). The water is now translucent, so you can see the track through it, and its shoreline comes from the banks: it slips under the ground and fades across the road in a wavy line instead of a square sheet. This applies to every water splash.

data.reply: Damage now repairs itself. After 4 s without a knock every part recovers, so a battered car is good as new in about 20 s, and the dents ease back out.

data.reply: The machine gun now fires dead straight from the gun. It can swing up to about 15 degrees toward the car ahead, so point your car to aim. Rounds are thin glowing tracers, every shot gives a muzzle flash, a puff of smoke and an ejected brass casing, and the gun is now a six-barrel rotary that spins up and shakes as it fires.

data.reply: Good catch, a real bug. The Mountain Pass lap stopped 50 m short of the start line, so the road there was one stretched strip with no ground shaped under it, and the valleys ran over it. The lap now closes properly, and a new test checks every stage's road for gaps. Also, when a hillside hides the road just ahead of you, it now turns see-through too.

data.reply: Fixed on every tunnel. At each mouth the ground stepped up from the road to the hill over the tunnel, which made a sloping wall across the opening. That strip now sinks under the road, so the portal is open. A new test checks every tunnel mouth on every stage (four stages had it).

data.reply: Houses redone in four kinds: cottages, two-storey houses, tall townhouses with flat roofs, and shops with big windows, signs and awnings. Each has windows with sills on every floor, a door, chimneys, a gabled or hipped roof and a much wider range of colours. They also turn see-through when they block your view of the car.

data.reply: Two bugs, both fixed in the shared code, so every stage gets the fix. 1) The road here is itself a low bridge over the rail cutting, and pier placement ignored lower bridge decks, so a pier landed on it. 2) The ground under bridge decks was levelled to deck height and poked through. On your question: fixes do carry over, because they live in the shared terrain and bridge code. This spot just had a case the earlier fix didn't cover. New tests now check every stage for ground through any deck and piers on any road; they failed on seven stages before the fix.
